# `Q-9-3` — Mismatched XML End Tag

> A closing tag does not match the most recent open tag.

## What this means

XML is strictly nested: every `<a>` must close as `</a>`, and
elements must close in reverse opening order. This error fires
when the parser encounters a closing tag whose name does not
match what it was expecting. The message includes both the
expected and the found tag name, plus the location.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A missing closing tag** somewhere earlier in the document.
  The parser stayed inside the unclosed element and tripped
  on the next closing tag it saw.
- **A typo in the tag name** (`</nmae>` for `</name>`).
- **A copy-paste mistake** that pasted a closing tag without
  the matching opener.

## How to fix

The message names the unmatched closing tag — that is where the
parser stopped. Read backward from that point until you find
the element that was opened but never closed; that is the real
source of the problem.

If the closing tag is correct, an XML-aware editor (anything
that highlights matching tags) makes the missing opener stand
out.

## Related

- `Q-9-2` — unexpected end of input: the same nesting problem
  if it survives to the end of the document.
